skill.name: markitdown
skill.description: Convert PDFs, Office files, images, audio, web content, and structured data into Markdown using local, batch, OCR, transcription, and optional AI workflows.
skill.summary: Turn common document formats into structured Markdown for review, analysis, and LLM workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, placeholder credentials, fixed installation commands, and intended output writes. Confirmed risks include plaintext credential persistence or display, command-line key exposure, and optional document-image transfer to OpenRouter. The skill also directs agents to generate unrelated schematics through another skill by default.

remediation.issue: API key handling can expose credentials through shell profiles, terminal output, and command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove key-echo instructions and the --api-key option. Recommend session-scoped environment variables or an approved secret manager without plaintext persistence.

remediation.issue: AI-enhanced conversion can send document images to OpenRouter and downstream model providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit privacy warning and require confirmation before remote processing. Recommend local conversion for confidential, regulated, or proprietary documents.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md requests unrelated schematic generation through another skill by default.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the default generation instruction. Make cross-skill diagram creation an explicit, user-requested option with clear cost and data-sharing disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Document Image Processing Lacks a Privacy Warning
semantic_findings.description: The optional AI helper supplies a remote OpenRouter client while converting a local document. Users are not warned that extracted images may reach external model providers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The client is configured for OpenRouter and passed directly into MarkItDown before converting the local input. The script describes remote AI image analysis but provides no privacy confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Unrequested Cross-Skill Content Generation
semantic_findings.description: The conversion skill directs agents to use another skill and generate scientific schematics by default. This can create unrelated files, remote AI usage, and unexpected cost.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly says schematics should be generated by default and provides a generation command. This behavior is separate from converting existing files to Markdown.

content.value_statement: Manual extraction from mixed document formats is slow and inconsistent. This skill converts files into structured Markdown with local, batch, OCR, transcription, and optional AI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Converts PDFs, Office documents, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, EPUB, images, audio, and supported web sources into Markdown.
Extracts image text with OCR when the required system dependencies are installed.
Transcribes supported audio and YouTube content when the relevant optional dependencies are available.
Batch converts selected file types with configurable recursion, worker count, and output directory.
Organizes scientific papers by year and creates Markdown and catalog indexes.
Adds optional AI image descriptions through an OpenRouter-compatible client.
limitations: MarkItDown and format-specific dependencies must be installed before conversion.
Optional AI processing sends document images to remote providers and may incur usage costs.
Conversion fidelity depends on source quality, document structure, OCR accuracy, and supported metadata.
The scripts create new Markdown outputs but do not preserve every visual or interactive source feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Literature
use_cases.description: Convert paper collections into searchable Markdown with source metadata, year folders, and an index.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Documents
use_cases.description: Transform mixed Office files, PDFs, and web content into a consistent format for documentation systems.

use_cases.title: Build LLM Knowledge Sources
use_cases.description: Create structured Markdown from diverse source files before indexing, summarization, or retrieval workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert {input_file} to Markdown and save it as {output_file}. Preserve headings, lists, tables, links, and source metadata where available.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a faithful Markdown copy of one document.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert supported files in {input_directory} to {output_directory}. Include {extensions}, search {recursive_mode}, and report successful and failed conversions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs consistent Markdown from a folder of mixed files.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Research Papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert PDFs in {papers_directory} into {output_directory}. Organize results by year and create a literature index with source metadata.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher is preparing a literature review collection.

prompt_templates.title: Describe Document Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert {input_file} with AI image descriptions using {model} and {prompt_type}. Confirm remote processing is permitted before writing {output_file}.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs searchable descriptions for figures or slides.

output_examples.output: A Markdown document with the report title, section headings, paragraphs, lists, extracted tables, links, and source metadata.

output_examples.input: Batch convert all PDF and DOCX files in the policies folder.
output: Converted 18 supported files into the selected output directory.
Reported 17 successful conversions and one file requiring review.
Kept each source filename in the generated document metadata.

output_examples.input: Prepare a year-organized literature collection from research PDFs.
output_examples.output: Year folders containing converted papers, a Markdown literature index, and a catalog summarizing available source metadata.

best_practices: Review converted headings, tables, citations, and OCR text against the source before publication.
Use local conversion for sensitive files and enable remote AI processing only with explicit authorization.
Write results to a dedicated output directory and retain the original source files.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys in prompts, scripts, command arguments, shell history, or shared output.
Do not send confidential documents to OpenRouter, Azure, or other remote services without approval.
Do not enable unknown plugins or install dependencies from unverified repositories.

faq.question: Which file formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill documents support for PDFs, Office files, images, audio, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, EPUB, and YouTube sources.

faq.question: Does basic conversion require internet access?
faq.answer: Local file conversion usually does not. YouTube, Azure Document Intelligence, OpenRouter, package installation, and some transcription workflows require network access.

faq.question: Can I process confidential documents?
faq.answer: Use local conversion and review dependency behavior. Do not enable remote AI or cloud document services without organizational approval.

faq.question: How should I provide an OpenRouter API key?
faq.answer: Use a scoped environment variable for the current session or an approved secret manager. Avoid command arguments, shell profiles, logs, and prompts.

faq.question: Can the skill convert many files at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script supports extension filters, recursive discovery, configurable workers, and a selected output directory.

faq.question: Will the Markdown exactly match the source layout?
faq.answer: No. The output emphasizes structured text, tables, links, and metadata. Complex visual layouts, OCR, and interactive content may require manual correction.
